title: Transitive inference and the testing effect: Retrieval practice impairs  transitive inference.
authors: Mulligan, Neil W | Buchin, Zachary L | Powers, Annaliisa
corrected_evidence_type: empirical multi-experiment study with small internal meta-analysis
access_status: publisher abstract and supplementary material; main full text not openly retrieved
corpus_or_sample: 3 experiments plus a small meta-analysis combined with prior experiments
principal_findings: Retrieval practice improved neither the complex inference task nor its transfer; transitive inference was worse after retrieval practice than after restudy.
quantitative_summary: Small combined meta-analysis reported a negative testing effect on transitive inference, d=-0.37.
key_limitations: Laboratory paradigm and narrow reasoning task; not a systematic review; result concerns element-interactive inference and should not be generalized to ordinary factual retention.
next_action: Reclassify out of synthesis core; retain as a high-value contradictory empirical boundary condition.

title: Flashcards: The Preferred Online Game-Based Study Tool Self-Selected by Students  to Review Medical Histology Image Content.
authors: Mishall, Priti L | Burton, William | Risley, Michael
journal: Advances in experimental medicine and biology
corrected_evidence_type: descriptive longitudinal usage study / book chapter
access_status: abstract and institutional publication record; chapter full text not openly retrieved
domain_population: first-year medical students studying histology images
corpus_or_sample: usage data across four graduating classes (2018–2021) and four Quizlet study sets
mechanism_or_intervention: self-selected Quizlet modes for image-based histology review
comparison: relative use of Flashcards, Learn, Test, Match, Gravity and Speller modes
outcomes: tool use/preference; not direct learning or retention
principal_findings: Use increased over the four-year period and the Flashcards mode was selected more often than other Quizlet modes.
quantitative_summary: Mean usage rose from 445 in 2018 to 849 in 2021; mode-use difference p<0.0001 by chi-square.
key_limitations: Usage preference is not evidence of learning; no randomized comparator; product mode selection may reflect familiarity or interface convenience.
next_action: Reclassify out of synthesis core; use for related-systems and preference questions only.

title: Rad Path in a Flash: Creation of the First AMSER Sponsored Digital Flashcard Deck  and a Review of Digital Flashcard Use among? Medical Students.
authors: Hartman, Matthew | Debiec, Nicholas | Kim, Esther | Syed, Hamid | Adhya, Julie | Giardino, Angela | Hill, Jeanne
corrected_evidence_type: product-development study with pre/post confidence survey
access_status: publisher abstract and bibliographic record; full text not openly retrieved
corpus_or_sample: 185 general survey respondents; 31 pre/follow-up deck users
outcomes: use, perceived need, confidence and favorability
principal_findings: Digital flashcard use was common, students reported demand for a radiology deck, and confidence increased after using the deck.
quantitative_summary: 87.6% had used digital flashcards; 33.5% for radiology; 67.6% would use a society-sponsored deck; 31 paired respondents for deck confidence.
key_limitations: Confidence and acceptance are not learning outcomes; small follow-up sample; no randomized control; possible volunteer and sponsorship effects.
next_action: Reclassify out of synthesis core; retain for governance, content quality and institutional sponsorship questions.

title: Attitudes of an international student cohort to the Quizlet study system employed  in an advanced clinical health care review course.
authors: Zeitlin, Benjamin D | Sadhak, Nishanth D
domain_population: international graduate dental students in pharmacology review
mechanism_or_intervention: Quizlet electronic flashcards with spaced learning and self-testing
outcomes: ease of use, ease of study and acceptance
principal_findings: Students broadly accepted Quizlet and reported ease of use and study.
key_limitations: No objective retention measure or experimental comparator; small professional-course cohort; conclusions concern usability rather than effectiveness.
next_action: Reclassify out of synthesis core; retain as usability evidence.

title: The Use of Retrieval Practice in the Health Professions: A State-of-the-Art  Review.
authors: Serra, Michael J | Kaminske, Althea N | Nebel, Cynthia | Coppola, Kristen M
domain_population: medicine, nursing, dentistry and other health professions
corpus_or_sample: historical and thematic review; no systematic included-study count
mechanism_or_intervention: retrieval practice and its curricular/self-regulated adoption
comparison: not applicable as a systematic comparative synthesis
outcomes: historical adoption, applications, barriers and future directions
principal_findings: The review traces increasing adoption since the early 2000s, links growth to assessment-driven education and third-party resources, and highlights persistent barriers to learner uptake.
quantitative_summary: No pooled effect or exhaustive study count.
key_limitations: Narrative state-of-the-art method; selective evidence and chronology cannot establish effect size; strong claims rely partly on prior syntheses.
next_action: Retain as implementation/history source, not as independent effectiveness evidence.

title: Review of 3 Comprehensive Anki Flash Card Decks for Dermatology Residents.
corpus_or_sample: three publicly available Anki deck families
mechanism_or_intervention: pre-made dermatology Anki decks with image, free-response and cloze formats
comparison: qualitative comparison of scope, card format, updating, tags, access and cost
outcomes: coverage, usability, format and practical advantages/disadvantages
principal_findings: Decks differed substantially in size, coverage, card granularity, image use, update mechanisms and cost; long free-response slides and incomplete coverage were noted as limitations.
quantitative_summary: Deck sizes reported as approximately 13,833, 8,454 and 7,889 cards at the time of review.
key_limitations: Single-author expert assessment; no learner outcomes or formal quality rubric; decks and links change over time.
next_action: Reclassify out of synthesis core; retain for content-governance and card-design variables.

title: Retrieval Practice Improves Exam Performance as a Function of Review Question  Number and Format.
domain_population: 88 second-year Doctor of Physical Therapy students
corpus_or_sample: 42 baseline and 46 intervention-cohort students; 160 exam questions
comparison: no review and alternative question formats/numbers
outcomes: performance on later multiple-choice exam questions
principal_findings: Both formats improved performance over no review; after controlling for item difficulty, more than one multiple-choice review question outperformed a single open-ended review question, with little additional gain from a third item.
quantitative_summary: Two MCQs improved adjusted performance by about 5.1 percentage points and three by about 4.9 points versus open-ended review; effect appeared to saturate after two MCQs.
key_limitations: One programme and examination format; practice/final-test congruence favors MCQ; cohort and item-level design limits generalization to transfer or long-term retention.
next_action: Reclassify out of synthesis core; retain as direct parameter evidence.

title: The usefulness of retrieval practice and review-only practice for answering  conceptually related test questions.
authors: Pilotti, Maura | Chodorow, Martin | Petrov, Radoslav
access_status: abstract and publisher record; full text not openly retrieved
domain_population: higher-education students in simulated test preparation
corpus_or_sample: sample size not reported in accessible abstract
mechanism_or_intervention: retrieval practice with correctness checking versus question-and-answer review
outcomes: self-assessment, test performance and memory for conceptually related questions
principal_findings: Both retrieval and review-only practice improved self-assessment and performance on conceptually related questions; the abstract does not establish a unique retrieval advantage.
quantitative_summary: No effect size reported in accessible abstract.
key_limitations: Immediate last-minute preparation scenario; familiar domain; sample and detailed statistics unavailable; not a review.
next_action: Reclassify out of synthesis core; retrieve full text only if needed for comparator taxonomy.

title: Testing enhances learning: A review of the literature.
journal: Journal of professional nursing : official journal of the American Association of  Colleges of Nursing
access_status: publisher full-text sections accessible; no open reusable copy located
domain_population: professional and nursing education with cognitive-psychology foundations
corpus_or_sample: narrative search of ERIC, PsycINFO, PubMed and CINAHL; no systematic included-study count
comparison: testing versus study/restudy across cited literature
principal_findings: The review recommends answer production, repeated/expanding schedules and feedback and argues that testing remains underused.
key_limitations: Narrative selection and recommendation synthesis; does not quantify heterogeneity or risk of bias; older literature cutoff.
next_action: Retain as historical practice guidance, not as an independent quantitative synthesis.

title: Retrieval activates related words more than presentation.
corrected_evidence_type: three-experiment empirical study with internal mini-meta-analysis
access_status: publisher abstract/full-text link; extraction based on abstract
mechanism_or_intervention: retrieval versus presentation/restudy under varying target accessibility
principal_findings: Retrieval produced a small increase in mediator activation, but mediator activation was not reliably related to target accessibility.
quantitative_summary: Small positive internal meta-analytic effect; exact value not reported in accessible abstract.
key_limitations: Laboratory mechanism outcome rather than educational achievement; internal meta-analysis is not a systematic review; mediator account remained incomplete.
next_action: Reclassify out of synthesis core; retain as mechanistic evidence.

title: Mobile-Assisted Vocabulary Learning: A Review of Anki
access_status: ERIC abstract and bibliographic record; full text not openly retrieved
domain_population: English as a foreign language vocabulary learners
corpus_or_sample: no systematic corpus or search method reported in accessible record
mechanism_or_intervention: Anki mobile flashcards, spaced repetition and flexible study
outcomes: lexical retention and retrieval; user implications
principal_findings: The article presents Anki as potentially useful for vocabulary retention while acknowledging shortcomings.
quantitative_summary: No pooled estimate or included-study count.
key_limitations: Narrative product-focused review; evidence-selection method unclear; broad effectiveness language cannot be independently appraised from abstract.
next_action: Retain as related-system description; full text is low priority unless its cited corpus is needed.

title: Encouraging Students to Use Retrieval Practice: A Review of Emerging Research from Five Types of Interventions
access_status: ERIC abstract and publisher record; full text not openly retrieved
corpus_or_sample: emerging literature organized into five intervention types; count not reported in accessible abstract
mechanism_or_intervention: information, direct experience, reduced effort/errors, personal performance feedback and multifaceted planning/practice/reflection interventions
comparison: student choice to use or avoid retrieval practice
outcomes: adoption and self-regulated use of retrieval practice
principal_findings: Information or a one-time experience alone was insufficient; reducing effort/errors, providing personal benefit feedback and multifaceted sustained interventions appeared more promising.
key_limitations: Emerging, small literature; narrative organization; outcome is adoption rather than learning effectiveness.
next_action: Retain as central learner-control review; request full text if intervention details will directly define ARA parameters.

title: Retrieval Practice Can Improve Classroom Review Despite Low Practice Test Performance
authors: Leggett, Jack M. I. | Burt, Jennifer S. | Carroll, Annemaree
access_status: publisher full-text page and ERIC abstract
corpus_or_sample: sample size not stated in accessible abstract
mechanism_or_intervention: retrieval practice with feedback, with or without hints
principal_findings: Most students benefited from retrieval practice even when practice-test performance was low; hints sometimes improved learning by easing retrieval.
quantitative_summary: No effect size in accessible abstract.
key_limitations: Single school subject and age group; hints and feedback are intertwined; not a review.
next_action: Reclassify out of synthesis core; retain as direct evidence for hints, retrieval success and delayed testing.

title: WWC Quick Review of "Retrieval Practice Produces More Learning than Elaborative Studying with Concept Mapping"
corrected_evidence_type: secondary evidence review of one randomized study
domain_population: postsecondary students learning a science passage
corpus_or_sample: one primary randomized study; 40 students in the WWC-reviewed contrast
comparison: study once, repeated study and concept mapping
principal_findings: WWC rated the study as meeting standards without reservations and reported higher average test performance for retrieval practice.
quantitative_summary: Reported group averages: retrieval 67%, study once 27%, repeated study 49%, concept mapping 45%.
key_limitations: Not an independent primary study or synthesis; evaluates one publication; later critiques and re-examinations question condition equivalence and potential additional memorization.
product_or_mechanism: secondary appraisal of a primary experiment
next_action: Retain as quality-appraisal metadata, link to the primary study, and do not count as independent evidence.
